{{Mergingfrom |1=List of automobile manufacturers of China |target=Automobile manufacturers and brands of China |afd=List of automobile manufacturers of China |date =July 2026 }}There are currently about 150 active brands in the Chinese automobile market. Among them are 97 Chinese domestic brands and 43 joint venture (JV) brands.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Borucki |first=Matt |date=2023-12-12 |title=The polarisation of China's automobile production capacity |url=https://www.just-auto.com/analyst-comment/the-polarisation-of-chinas-automobile-production-capacity/ |access-date=2024-06-22 |website=Just Auto |language=en-US}}</ref> Before 2010, the traditional "Big Four" refers to the four major state-owned car manufacturers, [[SAIC Motor|SAIC]], [[FAW Group|FAW]], [[Dongfeng Motor Corporation|Dongfeng]] and [[Chang'an Automobile Group|Changan]]. Other Chinese car manufacturers, both from public and private sectors, like [[Geely Auto|Geely]], [[BAIC]], [[BYD Auto|BYD]], [[Chery]], [[GAC Group|GAC]], [[Great Wall Motor|Great Wall]], [[JAC Group|JAC]] and [[Seres (automobiles)|Seres]], emerged as the major players with the expansion of the Chinese [[automotive industry]].

The article is an introduction to major automobile manufacturers and brands of China; for the full list see ''[[List of automobile manufacturers of China]]''.

== Major manufacturers and brands ==
{{See also|List of automobile manufacturers of China}}
[[File:Chinese_major_auto_manufacturers_headquarters_locations.jpg|center|thumb|600x600px|Chinese major automobile manufacturers headquarter locations]]

=== Central state-owned manufacturers ===
''Central state-owned manufacturer'' refers to manufacturers directly owned by the [[State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission of the State Council]] (SASAC) of the [[China|People's Republic of China]].  Currently, [[FAW Group|FAW]], [[Dongfeng Motor Corporation|Dongfeng]] and [[Changan Automobile|Changan]] are owned and controlled by the Central Government.<ref>{{Cite web |title=（央 企）名录 －国务院国有资产监督管理委员会 |url=http://www.sasac.gov.cn/n2588045/n27271785/n27271792/index.html |access-date=2024-07-25 |website=www.sasac.gov.cn}}</ref> According to the [[Civil service of China|civil service ranks of China]], the central government controlled state-owned enterprises are ranked as Sub-Ministerial-Level Enterprise.
* '''[[FAW Group|FAW]]''' ('''China First Automobile Works Group Corporation''', {{Langx|zh|中国第一汽车集团有限公司|links=no}}) is a central state-owned automotive manufacturing company headquartered in [[Changchun]] which is directly under the control of the central government of China. Founded on 15 July 1953, it is the oldest car manufacturer of the People's Republic of China. Currently FAW sells products under their brands including [[Hongqi (marque)|Hongqi]], [[FAW Jiefang|Jiefang]], [[Bestune]] and [[Bestune|Yueyi]]. FAW also operates joint ventures with [[Toyota]], [[Volkswagen]] and [[Audi]].<ref name="Company Profile">{{cite web |title=Company Profile |url=http://www.faw.com/fawen/gyjt36/jtgl59/jtjj3/index.html}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Passing bumps in the road: what we can learn from FAW's 70-year journey-Xinhua |url=https://english.news.cn/20230715/e373851584c04489af5997ac1bca4508/c.html |access-date=2023-07-15 |website=english.news.cn}}</ref>
* '''[[Dongfeng Motor Corporation|Dongfeng]]''' ('''Dongfeng Motor Corporation''', {{Langx|zh|东风汽车集团有限公司|links=no}}) is a central state-owned automobile manufacturer headquartered in [[Wuhan]], [[Hubei]], which is directly under the control of the central government of China. Originally known as '''Second Automobile Works''' when it was founded in 1969, FAW and SAW were the two major manufacturers before the [[reform and opening up]] of China. It currently owns [[Voyah]], [[M-Hero]], [[Dongfeng Fengshen|Aeolus]], [[Forthing]], [[Dongfeng Nammi]] and operates joint ventures including [[Cummins]], [[Honda]], [[Nissan]], [[Infiniti]], and [[Stellantis]] ([[PSA Peugeot Citroën]]).<ref>{{cite web |title=Dongfeng Motor Corporation 东风汽车集团有限公司 – Dongfeng Motor Corporation 东风汽车集团有限公司 |url=https://www.dfm-global.com/col.jsp?id=144}}</ref>
* '''[[Changan Automobile|Changan]]''' ('''China Changan Automobile Group''', {{Langx|zh|中国长安汽车集团有限公司|links=no}}) is a central state-owned automobile manufacturer headquartered in [[Chongqing]]. It is the oldest automobile manufacturer in China, and can be traced back to 1862 during the [[Qing dynasty|Qing Dynasty]]. Changan designs, develops, manufactures and sells passenger cars sold under the Changan Auto, [[Deepal]], [[Avatr Technology|Avatr]] and Kaicene brands. Changan operates joint venture companies [[Ford Motor Company|Ford]] and [[Mazda]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=About Us - Changan International |url=http://www.globalchangan.com/about_us/}}</ref><ref name="hybrid">[https://www.reuters.com/article/idUSSHA13646320071216 China rolls out own hybrid car] reuters.com, Sat December 15, 2007 1:44am EST</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Narasimhan |first=T. E. |date=2016-07-09 |title=China's Changan revs up for India entry |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/china-s-oldest-automobile-company-and-state-owned-changan-automobile-eyes-tamil-nadu-ap-116070800328_1.html |access-date=2016-07-09 |website=www.business-standard.com |language=en}}</ref>

=== Local state-owned manufacturers ===
''Local state-owned manufacturers'' refers to manufacturers owned by the State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission of local governments (instead of the [[State Council of the People's Republic of China|State Council]]). Most local government-controlled manufacturers are ranked as Bureau-Director Level Enterprise or even lower level.
* '''[[SAIC Motor|SAIC]]''' ('''Shanghai Automotive Industry Corporation''', {{Langx|zh|上海汽车集团股份有限公司|links=no}}) is a Chinese state-owned automotive manufacturing company headquartered in [[Shanghai]]. It is controlled by the municipal government of Shanghai. SAIC sells vehicles under a variety of brands including [[IM Motors|IM]], [[Rising Auto]], [[Maxus]], [[MG Motor|MG]], [[Roewe]], [[Wuling Motors|Wuling]], [[Baojun]], and [[Yuejin]]. Joint venture brands include [[Buick]], [[Chevrolet]], [[Iveco]], [[Volkswagen]], and [[Audi]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=SAIC Motor Corp. Ltd. |url=https://asia.nikkei.com/Companies/SAIC-Motor-Corp.-Ltd |website=Nikkei Asia}}</ref>
* '''[[GAC Group|GAC]]''' ('''Guangzhou Automobile Corporation''', {{Langx|zh|广州汽车集团股份有限公司|links=no}}), is a Chinese state-owned automobile manufacturer headquartered in [[Guangzhou]] and controlled by the municipal government of Guangzhou. GAC sells passenger cars under the [[Trumpchi]], [[GAC Aion|Aion]], and [[Hyptec]] brands and operates foreign joint ventures with [[Honda]] and [[Toyota]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=关于我们-总览 - 广汽集团 |url=https://www.gac.com.cn/cn/about |access-date=2024-06-11 |website=www.gac.com.cn}}</ref>
* '''[[BAIC]]''' ('''Beijing Automotive Group Co., Ltd. ''', {{lang-zh|s=北京汽车集团有限公司|links=no}}), is a state-owned enterprise located in [[Beijing]] and controlled by the municipal government of [[Beijing]]. Its owns the brands of [[Arcfox]], [[BAIC Motor|Beijing]], [[BAIC Motor|Beijing Off-road]], and [[Foton Motor|Foton]]. It has foreign joint ventures with [[Hyundai Motor Company|Hyundai]] and [[Mercedes-Benz]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Into the Biac |url=http://www.baicgroup.com.cn/en/about}}</ref>
* '''[[JAC Motors|JAC]]''' ('''Anhui Jianghuai Automobile Group Corporation''', {{Langx|zh|安徽江淮汽车集团股份有限公司|links=no}}) is a state-owned enterprise based in [[Hefei]], [[Anhui Province]], and controlled by the Provincial Government of Anhui. It owns the brands of JAC Motors, JAC Yiwei, JAC Refine, and collaborates with Huawei under the [[Maextro]] brand.<ref name="intro">{{cite web |title=Introduction: JAC Motors – Coordinate Balance and Pursue Excellence |url=http://jacen.jac.com.cn/jac/showCatalogAction.do?method=print&catalogid=ff8080810f7564ef010f7a9c1e730045 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090213205907/http://jacen.jac.com.cn/jac/showCatalogAction.do?method=print&catalogid=ff8080810f7564ef010f7a9c1e730045 |archive-date=2009-02-13 |access-date=2011-03-20 |publisher=JAC Motors}}</ref>

=== State-private mixed ownership manufacturer ===

* '''[[Chery]]''' ('''Chery Automobile''', {{lang-zh|s=奇瑞汽车股份有限公司|links=no}}), previous state-owned automobile manufacturer based in Anhui and controlled by the municipal government of [[Wuhu]]. It was restructured into a state-private mixed ownership manufacturer in 2025. It sells cars under the Chery, [[Exeed]], [[Jetour]] and [[ICar (marque)|iCar]] brands. It also has [[Chery Jaguar Land Rover|a foreign joint venture]] with [[Jaguar Land Rover]] for the production of [[Jaguar Cars|Jaguar]] and [[Land Rover]] cars in China.<ref>{{Cite web |title=INTRODUCTION |url=https://www.cheryinternational.com/pc/aboutchery/introduction/index.shtml |access-date=2024-06-11 |website=www.cheryinternational.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=奇瑞IPO，胜利在望？ |url=https://auto.gasgoo.com/news/202503/7I70419952C109.shtml |access-date=2025-09-09 |website=auto.gasgoo.com}}</ref>
* '''[[Seres Group|Seres]]''' ('''Seres Group''', {{lang-zh|s=赛力斯集团股份有限公司|links=no}}), is one of the first [[Mixed economy|state-private mixed ownership]] manufacturer in China. Headquartered in [[Chongqing]], it is currently co-owned by the founder's family, the state-owned company [[Dongfeng Motor Corporation|Dongfeng]] and municipal government of Chongqing. It used to be famous for producing light commercial vehicles and budget passenger vehicles but is transforming to produce premium electric vehicles starting in 2021, after partnering with Chinese tech giant [[Huawei]]. It owns the brands of [[Seres (automobiles)|Seres]], [[AITO (marque)|AITO]], [[DFSK Motor|Fengon]], and [[DFSK Motor|DFSK]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=About - Seres Group Co., Ltd. |url=https://seres.cn/EnAbout.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240513173618/https://seres.cn/EnAbout.html |archive-date=2024-05-13 |access-date=2024-05-16 |website=seres.cn}}</ref>

=== Notable privately owned manufacturers ===

* '''[[BYD Auto|BYD]]''' ('''BYD Auto''', {{lang-zh|s=比亚迪汽车有限公司|links=no}}), is an automobile manufacturer based in [[Shenzhen]], founded by [[BYD Company]] which are known for their batteries. It is currently the largest electric vehicle manufacturer of the world. It operates brands such as BYD, [[Denza]], [[Fangchengbao]], [[Yangwang]], and [[Linghui]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=BYD Co. Ltd. |url=https://www.wsj.com/market-data/quotes/BYDDF/company-people |access-date=2024-05-10 |website=Wall Street Journal}}</ref>
* '''[[Geely]]''' ('''Zhejiang Geely Holding Group''', {{lang-zh|s=浙江吉利控股集团有限公司|links=no}}), is one of the biggest privately owned automobile manufacturers and is headquartered in [[Taizhou, Zhejiang]]. Currently one of the fastest growing automotive groups in the world, Geely is known for its ownership of the Swedish luxury car brand [[Volvo Cars]], its performance counterpart [[Polestar]], and the British sports car company [[Lotus Cars|Lotus]]. It also owns the brands of [[Geely Auto|Geely]], [[Livan Automotive|Livan]], [[Lynk & Co]], [[Zeekr]], [[Volvo Cars]], [[London Electric Vehicle Company|LEVC]], [[Farizon Auto|Farizon]], [[Jidu Auto|Ji Yue]], [[Proton Holdings|Proton]] and [[Smart (marque)|Smart]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=About the Group – 吉利控股集团官网 |url=https://zgh.com/call-to-action-grid/about-the-group/ |access-date=2024-06-11 |language=zh-hans}}</ref>
* '''[[Great Wall Motor|GWM]]''' ('''Great Wall Motor''', {{lang-zh|s=长城汽车股份有限公司|links=no}}), is a private company famous for manufacturing [[Sport utility vehicle|SUVs]] headquartered in [[Baoding, Hebei]]. GWM sells vehicles under the brands of [[Haval (marque)|Haval]], [[Wey (marque)|Wey]], [[Tank (marque)|Tank]] and [[Ora (marque)|Ora]]. It operates a joint venture called [[Spotlight Automotive]] with [[BMW Group]] to produce [[Mini (marque)|Mini]] brand electric cars.<ref>{{Cite web |title=About GWM - GWM |url=https://www.gwm-global.com/aboutGWM/ |access-date=2024-06-11 |website=www.gwm-global.com}}</ref>
* '''[[Leapmotor]]''' ('''Zhejiang Leapmotor Technology''', {{Langx|zh|浙江零跑科技股份有限公司|links=no}}) is an EV manufacturer founded in 2015, headquartered in [[Hangzhou]]. [[Stellantis]] acquired a 20% stake in Leapmotor in 2023.
* '''[[Li Auto]]''' ('''Beijing Car And Home Information Technology''', {{Langx|zh|北京车和家信息技术有限公司|links=no}}) is a manufacturer founded in 2015. It specializes in developing and manufacturing premium [[Extended-range electric vehicle|range-extender]] electric vehicles and has rapidly grown into a major player in the Chinese automobile market.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Li Auto Profile |url=https://ir.lixiang.com/company-profile-0 |website=Li Auto official}}</ref>
* '''[[XPeng]]''' ('''Guangzhou Xiaopeng Motors Technology''', {{Langx|zh|广州小鹏汽车科技有限公司|links=no}}) is an EV manufacturer founded in 2014 and headquartered in [[Guangzhou]]. Together with [[Nio Inc.|Nio]] and [[Li Auto]], it is one of the first EV companies in China. [[Volkswagen Group]] acquired a 5% stake in XPeng in 2023.
* '''[[Xiaomi Auto]]''' ('''Xiaomi Automobile Co., Ltd''', {{Langx|zh|小米汽车有限公司|links=no}}) is the subsidiary of Chinese consumer electronics giant [[Xiaomi]] that produces EVs. It was founded in 2021 in Beijing and launched its first product, the [[Xiaomi SU7]], in 2024. Xiaomi is currently the only Chinese tech company that is directly involved in automotive manufacturing.
* '''[[Nio Inc.|Nio]]''' ('''Shanghai Nio Automobile''', {{Langx|zh|上海蔚来汽车有限公司|links=no}}) is an EV manufacturer founded in 2014 and headquartered in [[Shanghai]]. The company is noted for its [[Battery swapping|battery-swapping]] stations and premium EV. The company launched an entry-level brand, [[Onvo]], and the high-end brand [[Firefly (marque)|Firefly]] in 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Nio's Alps sub-brand has its official name revealed through new spy shots |url=https://www.arenaev.com/nios_alps_subbrand_has_its_official_name_revealed_through_new_spy_shots-news-3277.php |access-date=2024-09-21 |website=ArenaEV.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

=== Foreign and joint venture manufacturers ===
{{See also|List of automobile manufacturers of China#Foreign joint ventures/brands}}

Following the [[reform and opening up]], from 1994 to 2018, Chinese automotive policy mandated that foreign carmakers had to establish joint ventures (JVs) with a Chinese counterpart to produce vehicles in the country, with the Chinese partner owning at least 50% of the venture. This measure was implemented to protect local manufacturers and provide it with the chance to bridge the technology gap and develop their brands.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2018-04-18 |title=Autovista24 - China to drop 50:50 rule and allow foreign majorities in joint ventures |url=https://autovista24.autovistagroup.com/news/china-drop-5050-rule-and-allow-foreign-majorities-joint-ventures/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240522031843/https://autovista24.autovistagroup.com/news/china-drop-5050-rule-and-allow-foreign-majorities-joint-ventures/ |archive-date=2024-05-22 |access-date=2024-04-10 |website=Autovista24 |language=en-GB}}</ref>

On April 17, 2018, the [[National Development and Reform Commission]] (NDRC) of China announced that foreign ownership limits on automakers would be phased out over a five-year period.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2018-04-18 |title=China's Auto Industry: Foreign Ownership Limits Scrapped |url=https://www.china-briefing.com/news/chinas-auto-industry-foreign-ownership-limits-scrapped/ |access-date=2024-05-17 |website=China Briefing News |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last1=Zhang |first1=Albee |last2=McMorrow |first2=Ryan |title=China to relax foreign ownership limits on cars, other industries (Update) |url=https://phys.org/news/2018-04-china-foreign-ownership-limits-automakers.html |access-date=2024-05-17 |website=[[Phys.org]] |language=en}}</ref> On 28 July 2018, China lifted foreign ownership restrictions on new energy vehicle production, which benefited American electric car manufacturer [[Tesla, Inc.|Tesla, Inc]]. The company established a plant in Shanghai, becoming the first foreign automaker to open a wholly owned manufacturing facility in China.<ref name="China Rolls Closer to Relaxed Ownership Rules for Foreign Electric-Car Makers - Caixin Global">{{Cite web |title=China Rolls Closer to Relaxed Ownership Rules for Foreign Electric-Car Makers |url=https://www.caixinglobal.com/2017-09-20/china-rolls-closer-to-relaxed-ownership-rules-for-foreign-electric-car-makers-101147935.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231003145114/https://www.caixinglobal.com/2017-09-20/china-rolls-closer-to-relaxed-ownership-rules-for-foreign-electric-car-makers-101147935.html |archive-date=2023-10-03 |access-date=2023-09-17 |website=[[Caixin]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last1=Schaub |first1=Mark |last2=Atticus |first2=Zhao |date=2020-04-14 |title=The Impact Of China Removal Of Foreign Ownership Restrictions In Auto Sector |url=https://www.kwm.com/de/en/insights/latest-thinking/impact-of-china-removal-of-foreign-ownership-restrictions-in-auto-sector.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230423121131/https://www.kwm.com/de/en/insights/latest-thinking/impact-of-china-removal-of-foreign-ownership-restrictions-in-auto-sector.html |archive-date=2023-04-23 |access-date=2024-04-10 |website=King & Wood Mallesons}}</ref> The liberalization was followed by commercial vehicles in 2020 and passenger cars in 2022. The rule prohibiting foreign automakers from setting up more than two joint ventures in China was also lifted in 2022. Therefore, it became legally possible for foreign automakers to buy out local partners from joint ventures. In the 1990s, Chinese automakers pursued Western technology through joint ventures. However, a reversal occurred in the 2020s, with Western manufacturers now seeking technological assistance from Chinese counterparts and invested in China through joint ventures.<ref name=":18">{{Cite web |title=China's automotive odyssey: From joint ventures to global EV dominance |url=https://www.imd.org/ibyimd/innovation/chinas-automotive-odyssey-from-joint-ventures-to-global-ev-dominance/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240515072655/https://www.imd.org/ibyimd/innovation/chinas-automotive-odyssey-from-joint-ventures-to-global-ev-dominance/ |archive-date=2024-05-15 |access-date=2024-05-15 |website=IMD|date=26 January 2024 }}</ref> Several Chinese electric vehicle startups have leveraged their technological advantages, attracting investments from traditional Western automotive giants such as [[Renault]]-[[Nissan]], [[Volkswagen|VW]], [[BMW]], [[Mercedes-Benz]], [[Toyota]] and [[Stellantis]].

== Chinese technology industry involvement in the automotive industry ==
Since the 2020s, Chinese technology corporations such as [[Huawei]], [[Baidu]], and [[DJI]], with their advanced software or hardware technological capabilities, started entering the automotive business through various approaches.

[[Huawei Intelligent Automotive Solution|Huawei's partnership with automobile manufacturers]] has taken the form of three business models, from the standardized parts supply model, the "Huawei Inside" (HI) model, and the [[Harmony Intelligent Mobility Alliance]] (HIMA).<ref name=":322">{{Cite web |title=鸿蒙智行官网上线，成员包括问界、智界汽车 - IT之家 |url=https://www.ithome.com/0/733/537.htm |access-date=2023-11-19 |website=www.ithome.com}}</ref><ref name=":42">{{Cite web |title=华为申请注册"智界""LUXEED"商标 智界S7即将上市 - 手机中国 - |url=https://internet.cnmo.com/event/758601.html |access-date=2023-11-19 |website=internet.cnmo.com}}</ref> Baidu and DJI have provided autonomous driving system and hardware to automotive manufacturers.<ref name=":232">{{Cite web |title=New VOYAH FREE carrying Baidu Apollo's intelligent driving package hits market |url=https://autonews.gasgoo.com/m/70027527.html |date=2023-08-21 |access-date=2024-01-17 |website=autonews.gasgoo.com |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240117004822/https://autonews.gasgoo.com/m/70027527.html |archive-date=2024-01-17 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Pandaily |date=2022-06-09 |title=SGMW and DJI Jointly Develop Cars |url=https://pandaily.com/sgmw-and-dji-jointly-develop-cars/ |access-date=2024-01-17 |website=Pandaily |language=en-US}}</ref> [[Qihoo 360]] invested in the Chinese EV startup company [[Hozon Auto]].<ref name=":242">{{Cite web |title=Geely Holding and Baidu launch new AI-powered EV |url=https://www.chinadaily.com.cn/a/202310/30/WS653f114aa31090682a5eb674.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240117004823/https://www.chinadaily.com.cn/a/202310/30/WS653f114aa31090682a5eb674.html |archive-date=2024-01-17 |access-date= |website=[[China Daily]]}}</ref> [[Geely]] collaborates with Baidu to set up joint venture brands, and acquired Chinese smartphone company [[Meizu]] for its [[Polestar]] and [[Lynk & Co]] brands with its auto [[Operating system|OS]] and [[Augmented reality|AR system]]. [[Oppo]] collaborates with [[SAIC Motor]] on the [[infotainment system]] used for [[MG Motor|MG]] EVs. [[Xiaomi]] is the first and the only Chinese tech company that is [[Xiaomi Auto|directly involved in automotive design, development and manufacturing]], and operates its factory in Beijing.<ref name=":252">{{Cite web |title=Xiaomi to open car plant in Beijing with annual output of 300,000 vehicles |url=https://www.reuters.com/technology/xiaomi-open-car-plant-beijing-with-annual-output-300000-vehicles-beijing-govt-2021-11-27/ |website=[[Reuters]]|date=27 November 2021 }}</ref>

=== Major autonomous driving solution companies ===

* '''[[Yinwang]] (Shenzhen Yinwang Intelligent Technology Co., Ltd''', {{lang-zh|s=深圳引望智能技术有限公司}})  is a company of Huawei which specialized in providing parts and hardware and software solutions for automotive manufacturers. The company was formerly known as '''Huawei Intelligent Automotive Solution''' (HIAS, {{lang-zh|s=华为智能汽车解决方案}}), the automobile business unit of Huawei.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Huawei Launches New Software Brand for Intelligent Driving |url=https://english.aawsat.com/node/4982116 |access-date=2024-04-25 |website=english.aawsat.com |language=en}}</ref> The company is deeply involved in China's automotive industry, providing autonomous driving solutions for most manufacturers and brands.
* '''[[Momenta]]''' ('''Momenta Global Limited''') is a developer of autonomous driving technology based in [[Beijing]] and [[Suzhou, Jiangsu|Suzhou]].  Founded in 2016, it is backed and invested by multiple manufacturers including [[SAIC Motor|SAIC]], [[General Motors|GM]], [[Toyota]] and [[Mercedes-Benz]].<ref name=":02">{{Cite web |author=Pan Yue |date=2017-07-25 |title=NIO Capital Leads $46M Round In Autonomous Driving Technology Firm Momenta |url=https://www.chinamoneynetwork.com/2017/07/25/nio-capital-leads-46m-round-in-autonomous-driving-technology-firm-momenta |archive-url= |archive-date= |access-date=2018-07-05 |work=China Money Network}}</ref>
* '''[[Qianli Technology]] (Chongqing Qianli Technology Co., Ltd''' [[Chinese language|Chinese]]: 重庆千里科技股份有限公司), formerly known as '''Lifan Technology (Group) Co., Ltd.''' (力帆科技（集团）股份有限公司), is a Chinese technology company specializing in the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and automotive technologies. Headquartered in Chongqing, the companies is mostly owned by [[Geely]] and is the major provider of  autonomous driving solution for the Geely Group.
* '''[[Zhuoyu Technology]]''' ('''Shenzhen Zhuoyu Technology Co., Ltd,''' {{Lang-zh|s=卓驭科技}}), formerly known as '''DJI Automotive''', is an autonomous driving solution company invested by [[FAW Group]] and [[DJI]]. The company was originally established as DJI's automotive division in 2016 before being spun off as an independent entity in 2023.
* '''[[Horizon Robotics]]''' ({{Lang-zh|c=|s=地平线}}) is a Chinese technology company headquartered in [[Beijing]]. The company develops [[artificial intelligence]] (AI) chips used in [[self-driving car]]s and [[Advanced driver-assistance system|advanced driver assistance systems]] (ADAS). The company is the major autonomous driving solution provider of [[Li Auto]], [[SAIC Motor|SAIC]], [[BYD Auto|BYD]] and [[Chery]].
* '''[[DeepRoute.ai]]''' (Chinese:元戎启行), is a Chinese autonomous driving company founded in 2019 and headquartered in Shenzhen, China. The company is invested and backed by [[Great Wall Motor|GWM]].
